subtitle: Wishes, polite requests and advice with würde
words.intro: Sylt is where rich Germans go to be windblown. It has thatched roofs, oysters, and hotel guests who have rather clear ideas about what would be better.

grammar[0].blocks[2].title: Words for the practice page
grammar[0].fact: Germans complain in a very specific way: you do not raise your voice, you cite the rule. *Laut Prospekt* says the brochure. Courts have ruled on a table for holiday complaints, the *Frankfurter Tabelle*, listing how much of your money you get back for noise, cold pool or missing sea view.

grammar[1].subheading: The polite one-word forms, and giving advice
grammar[1].blocks[0].title: würde or one word?
grammar[1].blocks[1].title: Polite and useful
grammar[1].blocks[1].rows[2][2]: Would you close the window, please?
grammar[1].blocks[1].rows[4][2]: If I were you, I’d see a doctor.
grammar[1].blocks[1].note: With sein, haben and the helpers use the one word: *wäre, hätte, könnte*. With everything else, use *würde*.
grammar[1].blocks[2].title: Complaining politely
grammar[1].blocks[2].text: *Ich hätte da ein Problem.* I have a little problem. Say it with a small smile, and it’s the best opening in German. Then: *Könnten Sie das bitte prüfen?*
grammar[1].fact: The Hindenburgdamm joined Sylt to the mainland in 1927. It carries only a railway, so cars ride on a flat train wagon for the last 11 km, with their drivers sitting inside them.

listen.intro: Polite requests, line by line. Hear each one, say it after the voice, and then use it on a hotel you have stayed in.
speak.intro: What would you like, what would you change? Tell the tutor about your dream holiday, with würde.

document.intro: A real painted sign on a hotel wall. It only has a few words, and a beer mug. Read it, then be a difficult guest about it.
document.fact: A *Bierkeller* really was a cellar: before fridges, beer was kept cool underground, and the trees planted above it to keep it cool gave us the beer garden. And *alkoholfrei* is big business: Germany sells a great deal of alcohol-free beer.
document.tasks[1].instruction: Make it polite with würde, könnte or hätte.
reading.intro: Frau Huber has won a weekend on Sylt, in a very elegant hotel, in a raffle at the butcher’s. She has taken Maya along, and she has never stayed in a hotel before. She has ideas. The young man at reception is called Jannik, and it is his first week.
reading.photos[1].caption: Ein Zimmer mit Meerblick. Das Meer ist gratis, der Blick nicht.
reading.fact: Sylt has beach chairs, wandering dunes, and a train across a causeway, because there is no road. The North Sea steadily carries away its west coast, so sand is pumped back every year.
reading.tasks[1].instruction: Make each sentence polite with würde, könnte or hätte.
reading.tasks[1].items[0].answer: Ich würde gern das Zimmer wechseln.
